# Benchmarks: Strut and OpenSees

<!-- Auto-generated by scripts/plot_markdown_benchmarks.py -->

Measured 2026-11-26 on AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (8 cores), OpenSees 3.7.1, Mojo 0.25.6.1 (4a162eab).
Times are the analysis only (OpenSees `analyze`/`eigen`, Strut solve phase), with recorders removed.

`opensees` is OpenSees, `strut` is Strut on one thread, and `strut-8` is Strut on 8 threads.

| Model | Free DOFs | opensees | strut | strut-8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `megatall_model1_40steps` | 162,624 | 833.5 s | 66.4 s (**12.5x faster**) | 27.5 s (**30.3x faster**) |
| `rc_frame3d_force_5x5x8` | 1,728 | 5.33 s | 2.12 s (**2.5x faster**) | 0.903 s (**5.9x faster**) |
| `rc_frame3d_disp_pdelta_5x5x8` | 1,728 | 5.52 s | 1.43 s (**3.8x faster**) | 0.885 s (**6.2x faster**) |
| OpenSees examples, all 38 cases | up to 167 | 16.4 s | 2.36 s (**6.9x faster**) | 2.35 s (**7.0x faster**) |

## OpenSees examples

38 cases, slowest first. Median of 3 runs per engine. Strut is faster in 21 and slower in 15. None is large enough to reach the threaded code, so `strut` and `strut-8` take the same time.
